subject: Throughput profile and SLO clarifications for ParcelFlow pilot
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sylvia Tran <sylvia.tran@parcelflow.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: throughput & SLOs from today’s discovery

Thanks again for the call this morning — good conversation. I wanted to capture the performance/profile points we discussed and confirm next steps so the sizing team can start a provisional plan. TL;DR: we heard bursty flash-sale traffic (~30s–2m bursts) and persistent streaming sessions; we need to validate tokens/sec and concurrency tradeoffs.

Summary of what we heard (please correct if I’ve mis-stated):
- Baseline steady traffic: ~25 qps (mostly short inference requests, non-streaming).
- Peak bursts: brief spikes up to ~300 qps (30–120s windows) during promos.
- Avg tokens per request: ~512 tokens (customer estimate), with the top 5% requests hitting ~2k tokens.
- Streaming: ~60 concurrent streaming sessions during peaks; these are low-bandwidth token streams but require first-byte streaming latency <=150ms and overall responsive tail behavior.
- SLO targets you’d like: p95 end-to-end latency (non-streaming) <= 400ms, first-byte streaming <= 150ms, and no more than 1% request error rate during bursts.

Questions / clarifications we asked we still need from ParcelFlow so we can size properly:
1) Can you confirm the distribution (percentiles) of request token lengths (p50/p90/p99)?
2) Are the burst windows frequent (multiple per hour) or rare (few-per-day)?
3) Do streaming sessions frequently upgrade to longer token dialogs (i.e., start streaming then request long completions)?
4) Any regulatory constraints (traffic locality, VPC-only) that would change where we place capacity?

Next steps (proposed):
- ParcelFlow: share a 24–72 hour sample of anonymized request logs or a small CSV sample with timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, streaming_flag. (Attachment stub: pf_token_profile.csv)
- Redwood: we’ll run a quick back-of-envelope sizing and propose an initial capacity plan (steady + autoscale config) and a short performance verification plan.
- Schedule a 60m technical follow-up with ParcelFlow eng-ops + Redwood infra (suggested window: Tue 12/1 10:00–11:00 PT).

I’ll loop in Neha and Monica for the sizing; Neha — can you take point on a provisional GPU / pod recommendation once we have the sample?

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

[Attachment: pf_token_profile.csv (text/csv) — sample schema suggested: timestamp, request_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, streaming_flag]

From: Sylvia Tran <sylvia.tran@parcelflow.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: eng-ops@parcelflow.com
Date: Sat, 27 Nov 2027 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: throughput & SLOs from today’s discovery

Thanks Marcus — that matches what we said. Quick clarifications and I attached the small sample slice you requested.

Clarifications:
- p50 tokens_in: 480, p90: 1,020, p99: 1,900.
- Burst cadence: ~2–3 bursts per hour during market hours (each ~45–90s). We also have a few larger promotional days that can generate sustained higher loads for ~10–20 minutes.
- Streaming behavior: streaming sessions generally remain streaming for the session lifespan (~30–120s), with ~10% of streams escalating to longer completions.
- Data location: US-only, VPC peering is required for the pilot.

Attached: parcelflow_workload_sample.tsv (anonymized 48h sample). The file is small (3MB) and contains the columns you suggested.

We can do Tue 12/1 10:00 PT — looping in our eng-ops alias.

Best,
Sylvia
Head of ML Platform | ParcelFlow
sylvia.tran@parcelflow.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Recap: throughput & SLOs from today’s discovery

Thanks for the recap. A couple of internal sizing clarifications before we produce a provisional plan:
- Model selection influence: which model family are they planning to run? We should assume a 7B-class open model for initial sizing unless they specify otherwise. That changes GPU memory / kv-cache footprint and batch sizing.
- Quantization tolerance: ask if ParcelFlow is open to int8 quantization for inference — that will materially reduce GPU memory and increase packing efficiency for high qps bursts.
- Streaming concurrency: streaming sessions are expensive for slot occupancy; confirm how we treat partial-token eviction and kv-cache retention for short bursts.

I’ll start a quick sim assuming 7B @ int8 and per-request avg 512 tokens. Marcus — can you confirm whether we should assume continuous KV cache or ephemeral per-request?

Neha
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sylvia Tran <sylvia.tran@parcelflow.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, eng-ops@parcelflow.com
Date: Sun, 28 Nov 2027 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed provisional sizing + next steps (ParcelFlow pilot)

Appreciate the sample data, Sylvia — reviewed the TSV quickly and it aligns with the percentile numbers you sent. Based on the initial assumptions (7B-class model, int8 quantization allowed, avg 512 tokens/request), here’s a provisional sizing and playbook we recommend: 

Provisional sizing (back-of-envelope):
- Steady capacity: target to sustain ~25 qps -> equivalent to 2 x A10G-equivalent pods for baseline routing and low-latency non-streaming.
- Burst handling: autoscale policy to add capacity for short bursts up to ~300 qps (30–120s). We estimate needing additional ~12 A10G-equivalent GPUs for full-burst headroom if using naive single-request routing. With batching + prefix caching we think we can reduce that to ~6–8 GPUs for the 30–90s bursts.
- Streaming: reserve lightweight streaming slots; estimate 8 stream-handling workers to support ~60 concurrent streams with acceptable first-byte latency. If streams escalate to long completions (top 10%), autoscale to spillover inference pods.

Notes and assumptions:
- Quantization: int8 recommended for initial pilot; if ParcelFlow cannot accept int8 we’ll reassess and add ~20–30% capacity headroom for int16.
- Batching: we’ll enable latency-aware batching with a max queue wait of 25ms to balance throughput and p95 latency.
- Caching: prefix + KV caching on repeated prompts expected to save ~15–35% tokens during promos (based on their sample).
- Network / locality: VPC peering OK — plan to stage pilot in us-west with dedicated capacity for lower variance.

Performance verification plan (short):
1) Redwood will provision the steady capacity (2 pods) in a staging VPC and run a synthetic replay using the provided TSV to validate p95 latencies and error rates.
2) Run 3 burst tests (30s, 90s, 10min scaled) to validate autoscale/hot-start behavior.
3) Capture token/sec and per-request latency heatmaps; produce a remediation list if p95 > 400ms.

Action items / next steps:
- ParcelFlow: confirm model family (7B vs 13B) and whether int8 quant is acceptable. Also please confirm the HubSpot deal record (I linked one in the metadata).
- Redwood: Neha to bake up the exact GPU counts with cost estimates and Monica to draft the test harness and runbook.
- Schedule: Tue 12/1 10:00 PT for the technical deep-dive (I’ll send a calendar invite).

If this plan looks good, we’ll convert it to a short statement-of-work for the pilot and schedule the perf tests.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
